headline: High: shared filesystem/MCP and permissive tool use create prompt-injection, leakage, and write-conflict risks; TREK’s sensitive travel data can flow into Windsurf’s broader editor context.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: TREK can use MCP and browsers, and Windsurf can read clipboard/filesystem and use MCP, so a shared channel exists where TREK content could be treated as instructions by Windsurf. Windsurf’s editor-process tool loop and TREK’s real-time collaborative outputs make injection plausible without extra setup.
conditions: IF TREK content is copied into Windsurf via clipboard or shared files, THEN prompt-like text can influence tool use.
IF both agents connect to the same MCP server, THEN untrusted TREK output can be parsed as instructions.
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents.
Use separate MCP servers or disable MCP on one side.
Add a manual review step before Windsurf executes any TREK-derived text.
Prefix imported TREK content as data, not instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for cross-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK touches reservations, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets, while Windsurf reads and writes workspace files and has broad network egress. Because Windsurf can access local filesystem state and TREK stores data in files, sensitive travel data can leak into Windsurf’s context and then out through its model proxy or networked tools.
conditions: IF TREK data is stored in shared local files, THEN Windsurf can read sensitive records.
IF Windsurf forwards workspace content to its model proxy, THEN TREK secrets can leave the local machine.
mitigations: Move TREK data to a separate user account or directory.
Exclude TREK files from Windsurf workspace indexing.
Rotate any exposed API keys or MFA secrets.
Restrict Windsurf network egress to approved destinations only.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can use MCP, and Windsurf can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses while TREK is collaborative and file-backed. That creates a direct write-write conflict path on shared resources, especially if TREK data or project files are co-located with Windsurf workspaces.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory, THEN concurrent writes can corrupt files or git state.
IF both agents target the same MCP-backed resource, THEN conflicting mutations can occur without locking.
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate workspace directory.
Disable auto-execute for Windsurf during shared edits.
Use git locks or a single-writer workflow.
Pause one agent before the other writes shared files.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK produces travel plans, budgets, reservations, and documents that Windsurf could ingest as authoritative context. Windsurf’s agentic loop can then act on those outputs with shell or file operations, so a mistaken TREK artifact can cascade into incorrect code or file changes. The path exists, but verification and approval controls reduce the blast radius.
conditions: IF Windsurf consumes TREK-generated text without verification, THEN downstream actions may be based on false premises.
IF Windsurf auto-execute is enabled, THEN erroneous TREK output can trigger immediate actions.
mitigations: Require human review of TREK outputs before reuse.
Keep Windsurf auto-execute disabled.
Use a checklist to verify reservations and confirmation numbers.
Limit TREK-derived inputs to read-only notes.
requires-engineering: add structured validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles country visit history, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets, while Windsurf is a closed-source editor agent with model-proxy egress and local-file access. That creates a plausible residency/retention mismatch for sensitive travel data, even though no specific jurisdictional mismatch is documented in the profiles.
conditions: IF TREK stores regulated travel or identity data in files opened by Windsurf, THEN retention and residency controls may diverge.
IF Windsurf sends workspace content to its model proxy, THEN data may leave the intended compliance boundary.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Windsurf-opened workspaces.
Redact confirmation numbers and secrets before sharing.
Review vendor retention and DPA terms before use.
Separate personal travel records from coding workspaces.
requires-engineering: implement data-class-based routing and retention controls.
